cast_dialogue.linea: Words travel, heroes, and when they travel, they change their clothes. Reported speech is the art of retelling.
Sofía called. She said she was tired, and she told me she couldn't come today.
She told me yesterday that she had missed the bus. She said she would call you later.
And Ben told me that he was preparing an exhibition. He said it would open the next day!
The neighbours said they were engaged. They told me they would celebrate here, in my garden!

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Reporting what someone said: 'say' (no person) vs 'tell + person'. Shift tenses one step back: present→past, past→past perfect, will→would, can→could. Time words shift too: today→that day, tomorrow→the next day, yesterday→the day before, here→there.

reading.texto: Sofía called Ben yesterday with news. She said she was tired because she had missed the bus and had walked home in the rain. She told him she couldn't meet them that day, but she would bring the music for the party. Ben told Kenji everything, and Kenji said he would cook ramen for everyone. Then Abuela Carmen phoned: she said she would bake her famous cake. Good news travels fast!
